39321-old-flies-in-new-dresses-how-to-dr.title: Old Flies In New Dresses How To Dress Dry Flies With The Win
39321-old-flies-in-new-dresses-how-to-dr.creator: Unknown
39321-old-flies-in-new-dresses-how-to-dr.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Though it would not be true to say that hitherto writers on fly-dressing have shown any lack of power of observation, still it is unfortunately true that their energy seems, strangely enough, to have stopped short at observing the natural fly, and has not been sufficient to carry them on to making even passable imitations, except of Ephemeridæ.

arxiv-2301-13721.title: DisDiff: Unsupervised Disentanglement of Diffusion Probabilistic Models
arxiv-2301-13721.creator: Tao Yang, Yuwang Wang, Yan Lu, Nanning Zheng yt14212@stu.xjtu.edu.cn
arxiv-2301-13721.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tao Yang, Yuwang Wang, Yan Lu, Nanning Zheng yt14212@stu.xjtu.edu.cn. Targeting to understand the underlying explainable factors behind observations and modeling the conditional generation process on these factors, we connect disentangled representation learning to Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DPMs) to take advantage of the remarkable modeling ability of DPMs.

arxiv-2305-03849.title: Polynomial superpotential for Grassmannian Gr ⁡ ( k , n ) \operatorname{Gr}(k,n) from a limit of vertex function
arxiv-2305-03849.creator: Andrey Smirnov ⋆ and Alexander Varchenko ⋄
arxiv-2305-03849.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Andrey Smirnov ⋆ and Alexander Varchenko ⋄. In this note we discuss an integral representation for the vertex function of the cotangent bundle over the Grassmannian, X = T ∗ ​ Gr ⁡ ( k , n ) X=T^{*}\operatorname{Gr}(k,n) . This integral representation can be used to compute the ℏ → ∞ \hbar\to\infty limit of the vertex function, where ℏ \hbar denotes the equivariant parameter of a torus acting on X X by dilating the cotangent fibers.

arxiv-2306-00151.title: Impact of Chiral-Transitions in Quantum Friction
arxiv-2306-00151.creator: Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Mário G. Silveirinha
arxiv-2306-00151.description: Abstract We theoretically investigate the role of chiral-transitions in the quantum friction force that acts on a two-level atom that moves with relative velocity v \displaystyle v parallel to a planar metallic surface. We find that the friction force has a component that is sensitive to the handedness of the atomic transition dipole moment.

arxiv-2306-07745.title: Kernelized Reinforcement Learning with Order Optimal Regret Bounds Thanks: Work was done when the author was affiliated with Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
arxiv-2306-07745.creator: Sattar Vakili, Julia Olkhovskaya
arxiv-2306-07745.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown empirical success in various real world settings with complex models and large state-action spaces. The existing analytical results, however, typically focus on settings with a small number of state-actions or simple models such as linearly modeled state-action value functions.

arxiv-2312-13211.title: DSFormer: Effective Compression of Text-Transformers by Dense-Sparse Weight Factorization
arxiv-2312-13211.creator: Rahul Chand*, Yashoteja Prabhu, Pratyush Kumar
arxiv-2312-13211.description: Abstract † † *Work completed during time at Microsoft Research With the tremendous success of large transformer models in natural language understanding, down-sizing them for cost-effective deployments has become critical. Recent studies have explored the low-rank weight factorization techniques which are efficient to train, and apply out-of-the-box to any transformer architecture.

arxiv-2312-16902.title: Joint Learning for Scattered Point Cloud Understanding with Hierarchical Self-Distillation
arxiv-2312-16902.creator: Kaiyue Zhou, Ming Dong, Peiyuan Zhi, Shengjin Wang
arxiv-2312-16902.description: Abstract Numerous point-cloud understanding techniques focus on whole entities and have succeeded in obtaining satisfactory results and limited sparsity tolerance. However, these methods are generally sensitive to incomplete point clouds that are scanned with flaws or large gaps. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end architecture that compensates for and identifies partial point clouds on the fly.

arxiv-2401-08025.title: Self-Imagine: Effective Unimodal Reasoning with Multimodal Models using Self-Imagination
arxiv-2401-08025.creator: Syeda Nahida Akter, Aman Madaan, Sangwu Lee, Yiming Yang, Eric Nyberg, Language Technologies Institute, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, United States, Department of Computer Science, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY, United States {sakter,amadaan}@cs.cmu.edu
arxiv-2401-08025.description: Abstract The potential of Vision-Language Models ( vlm s) often remains underutilized in handling complex text-based problems, particularly when these problems could benefit from visual representation. Resonating with humans’ ability to solve complex text-based problems by (1) creating a visual diagram from the problem and (2) deducing what steps they need to take to solve it, we propose Self-Imagine.

arxiv-2404-02909.title: A Comprehensive System for Secondary Structure Analysis of Protein Models
arxiv-2404-02909.creator: Vedh Ramalingam Kannan
arxiv-2404-02909.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Vedh Ramalingam Kannan. In protein structure analysis, the accurate characterization of secondary structure elements is crucial for understanding protein function and dynamics. This paper presents a software system designed for the comprehensive analysis of the secondary structure of protein models. Leveraging phi ( ϕ \phi ) and psi ( ψ \psi ) torsion angles, the system utilises K-means clustering and outlier detection techniques to identify and classify folding structures within protein models.

arxiv-2404-18487.title: Exponential synchronization of the Kuramoto model with inertia and frustration under locally coupled network Thanks: 1 1 School of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data, Hefei University, Hefei, China (ttzhud201880016@163.com) Thanks: 2 2 School of Mathematics and Statistics, Wuhan University, Wuhan,
arxiv-2404-18487.creator: Tingting Zhu 1, Xiongtao Zhang 2, *
arxiv-2404-18487.description: Abstract . We study the collective synchronized behavior of the Kuramoto model with inertia and frustration effects on a connected and symmetric network. We aim to establish sufficient frameworks for achieving complete frequency synchronization, taking into account initial configuration, small inertia and frustration, and large coupling strength.

arxiv-2405-08973.title: An adaptive approach to Bayesian Optimization with switching costs
arxiv-2405-08973.creator: Stefan Pricopie, Richard Allmendinger, Manuel López-Ibáñez, Clyde Fare, Matt Benatan, Joshua Knowles
arxiv-2405-08973.description: Abstract We investigate modifications to Bayesian Optimization for a resource-constrained setting of sequential experimental design where changes to certain design variables of the search space incur a switching cost. This models the scenario where there is a trade-off between evaluating more while maintaining the same setup, or switching and restricting the number of possible evaluations due to the incurred cost.

arxiv-2411-02248.title: Advancing Cyber-Attack Detection in Power Systems: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning and Graph Neural Network Approaches Thanks: This work was supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER) and performed at the Pacifi
arxiv-2411-02248.creator: Tianzhixi Yin, Syed Ahsan Raza Naqvi, Sai Pushpak Nandanoori, Soumya Kundu
arxiv-2411-02248.description: Abstract This paper explores the detection and localization of cyber-attacks on time-series measurements data in power systems, focusing on comparing conventional machine learning (ML) like k-means, deep learning method like autoencoder, and graph neural network (GNN)-based techniques. We assess the detection accuracy of these approaches and their potential to pinpoint the locations of specific sensor measurements under attack.

arxiv-2412-13708.title: JoVALE: Detecting Human Actions in Video Using Audiovisual and Language Contexts
arxiv-2412-13708.creator: Taein Son, Soo Won Seo, Jisong Kim, Seok Hwan Lee, Jun Won Choi
arxiv-2412-13708.description: Abstract Video Action Detection (VAD) entails localizing and categorizing action instances within videos, which inherently consist of diverse information sources such as audio, visual cues, and surrounding scene contexts. Leveraging this multi-modal information effectively for VAD poses a significant challenge, as the model must identify action-relevant cues with precision.

arxiv-2503-11752.title: BlackTHUNDER strikes twice: Balmer-line absorption in an overmassive Little Red Dot at z = 7.04 z=7.04
arxiv-2503-11752.creator: \orcidsymb Francesco D’Eugenio0000-0003-2388-8172, \orcidsymb Roberto Maiolino0000-0002-4985-3819, \orcidsymb Michele Perna0000-0002-0362-5941, \orcidsymb Hannah Übler0000-0003-4891-0794, \orcidsymb Xihan Ji0000-0002-1660-9502, \orcidsymb William McClymont0009-0009-5565-3790, \orcidsymb Sophie Koudm
arxiv-2503-11752.description: Abstract \jwst has revealed a population of ‘Little Red Dots’ (LRDs): compact, red objects at redshifts z = 2 ​ – ​ 9 z=2\text{--}9 with ‘v’-shaped spectral energy distributions, broad permitted lines, and, often, hydrogen Balmer absorption. We use NIRSpec/IFS data from the \blackthunder survey to study the H α line in the LRD Abell2744-QSO1 at z = 7.04 z=7.

arxiv-2505-11369.title: Compact, Large-Scale Photonic Neurons by Modulation-and-Weight Microring Resonators
arxiv-2505-11369.creator: *, Yuxin Wang, Joshua C. Lederman, Bhavin J. Shastri, *
arxiv-2505-11369.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by *, Yuxin Wang, Joshua C. Lederman, Bhavin J. Shastri, *. Fabrication imperfections, spatial constraints, and prohibitive costs collectively impede the scalability of neuromorphic photonics. In this work, we introduce a large-scale, compact photonic neuron in which each microring performs modulation and weighting simultaneously. This dual functionality is realized by leveraging both the carrier effect and thermal tunability, thereby merging modulation and weighting to conserve on-chip area, enhancing tuning efficiency, and capitalizing on wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) for scalable implementations.

arxiv-2509-23908.title: Post-disaster Max-Min Rate Optimization for Multi-UAV RSMA Network in Obstacle Environments Thanks: This work was supported in part by the Postdoctoral Fellowship Programs of CPSF (Nos. 2023TQ0256 and GZC20232056) and the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities (ZYTS25272).
arxiv-2509-23908.creator: Qingyang Wang, Zhuohui Yao, Wenchi Cheng, Xiao Zheng
arxiv-2509-23908.description: Abstract This paper proposes a rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) transmission scheme to maximize the minimum achievable rate among ground users for emergency communications in post-disaster scenarios with obstacles, with which the optimal positioning of multiple unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled base stations can be achieved timely. To address the resulting non-convex and intractable optimization problem, we design an alternating optimization approach.

arxiv-2602-12089.title: Choose Your Agent: Tradeoffs in Adopting AI Advisors, Coaches, and Delegates in Multi-Party Negotiation DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2602-12089.creator: Kehang Zhu, Nithum Thain, Vivian Tsai, James Wexler, Crystal Qian
arxiv-2602-12089.description: Abstract . As AI usage becomes more prevalent in social contexts, understanding agent-user interaction is critical to designing systems that improve both individual and group outcomes. We present an online behavioral experiment (N = 243) in which participants play three multi-turn bargaining games in groups of three.

arxiv-2603-21824.title: SteelDefectX: A Coarse-to-Fine Vision-Language Dataset and Benchmark for Generalizable Steel Surface Defect Detection
arxiv-2603-21824.creator: Shuxian Zhao Jie Gui Baosheng Yu Lu Dong Zhipeng Gui

britannica-1911-argenson.title: Argenson (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-argenson.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-argenson.description: Article 'Argenson' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 2), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. René de Voyer, seigneur d’Argenson (1596–1651), French statesman, was born on the 21st of November 1596. He was a lawyer by profession, and became successively avocat, councillor at the parlement of Paris, maître des requêtes, and councillor of state. Cardinal Richelieu entrusted him with several missions as inspector and intendant of the forces.

pmc-10604167.title: Genetic and Pharmacological Blockade of Sigma-1 Receptors Attenuates Inflammation-Associated Hypersensitivity during Acute Colitis in CD1 Mice
pmc-10604167.creator: Sergio López-Estévez, Mònica Aguilera, Georgia Gris, Beatriz de la Puente, Alicia Carceller, Vicente Martínez, Shao-Ming Wang
pmc-10604167.description: Sigma-1 receptors (σ1Rs) are implicated in nociception, including pain sensitization, and inflammation. We assessed the role of σ1Rs on acute colitis-associated hypersensitivity using both genetic (constitutive knockout) and pharmacological blockade of the receptor. Colitis was induced in CD1 wild-type (WT) and σ1R KO mice (exposure to dextran sodium sulfate, 3%).

pmc-10619608.title: A follow up on the feasibility after national implementation of magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection prior to preterm birth
pmc-10619608.creator: Sara Hellström, Andrea Jonsdotter, Maria Jonsson, Karin Pettersson, Sissel Saltvedt, Andreas Herbst, Johan Ågren, Ulrika Ådén, Magnus Domellöf, Henrik Hagberg, Ylva Carlsson
pmc-10619608.description: IntroductionThe risk for brain injury manifested as cerebral palsy is higher in very preterm born children than in term. Prenatal administration of magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) has been shown to be neuroprotective and reduces the proportion of very preterm born children later diagnosed with cerebral palsy.

pmc-10672193.title: The Impact of Chronic Kidney Disease on the Mortality Rates of Patients with Urological Cancers—An Analysis of a Uro-Oncology Database from Eastern Europe
pmc-10672193.creator: Mircea Ciorcan, Șerban Negru, Răzvan Bardan, Alin Cumpănaș, Iasmina Mattar, Yahya Bitar, Lazăr Chișavu, Luciana Marc, Adalbert Schiller, Adelina Mihăescu, Haruhito A Uchida
pmc-10672193.description: (1) Background: The relationship between chronic kidney disease (CKD) and urological cancers is complex, as most of these cancers are diagnosed in patients with advanced ages, when the kidney function may be already impaired. On the other hand, urological cancers could represent a risk factor for CKD, significantly reducing the life expectancy of the patients.

pmc-11330250.title: The Anti-Diabetic Effects of Medicinal Plants Belonging to the Liliaceae Family: Potential Alpha Glucosidase Inhibitors
pmc-11330250.creator: Tiara Ramadaini, Sri Adi Sumiwi, Ellin Febrina
pmc-11330250.description: BackgroundDiabetes mellitus is a complex metabolic disorder that has an enormous impact on people’s quality of life and health. Although there is no doubt about the effectiveness of oral hypoglycemic agents combined with lifestyle management in controlling diabetes, no individual has ever been reported to have been completely cured of the disease.

pmc-11428971.title: Differences between Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Patients with and without Epilepsy: The Results of a Quantitative Diffusion Tensor Imaging Study
pmc-11428971.creator: Anna B. Marcinkowska, Sergiusz Jóźwiak, Agnieszka Sabisz, Agnieszka Tarasewicz, Beata Rutkowska, Alicja Dębska-Ślizień, Edyta Szurowska
pmc-11428971.description: Introduction: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a neurocutaneous disease with a high incidence of epilepsy and damaging effects on cognitive development. To understand the mechanisms leading to abnormal cognitive development, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) techniques have begun to be used in recent years.

pmc-11555428.title: ﻿Cardaminezhangjiajieensis, a new species of Brassicaceae in China
pmc-11555428.creator: Jia-Lu Li, Cheng Zhang, Yi He, Quan-Ru Liu
pmc-11555428.description: ﻿AbstractCardaminezhangjiajieensis, a new species from Hunan Province, China, is described and illustrated. Cardaminezhangjiajieensis is similar to C.circaeoides. From the latter, C.zhangjiajieensis is readily distinguished by the terminal leaflet of the cauline leaf 4.5–7 cm (vs. 2.5–4.5 cm), mostly round or oblong (vs. oblong-oval to triangular-oval), margin undulating sinuses (vs. crenate or subentire), seed apically narrow wing (vs. wingless).

pmc-11667011.title: The molecular basis of pH sensing by the human fungal pathogen Candida albicans TOK potassium channel
pmc-11667011.creator: Rían W Manville, Claire L Illeck, Anthony Lewis, Zoe A McCrossan, Steven AN Goldstein, Geoffrey W Abbott
pmc-11667011.description: SummaryTwo-pore domain, outwardly rectifying potassium (TOK) channels are exclusively expressed in fungi. Human fungal pathogen TOK channels are potential antifungal targets, but TOK channel modulation in general is poorly understood. Here, we discovered that Candida albicans TOK (CaTOK) is regulated by extracellular pH, in contrast to TOK channels from other fungal species tested.

pmc-12420200.title: Hydrogen sulfide as a therapeutic agent for diabetic wounds: effects on inflammation and fibroblast pyroptosis
pmc-12420200.creator: Fusheng Zhao, Yuanyuan Li, Qunying Hu, Jiali Xu, Na Zhang, Yonglan Chen, Xinyue Jiang, Chunfu Gu, Kexin Zhang, Geng Wu
pmc-12420200.description: IntroductionChronic nonhealing wounds are one of the most serious complications of diabetes mellitus (DM), with limited treatment options. Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) plays a protective role against multiple inflammatory diseases. This study aimed to explore the effects of H2S on diabetic skin wound healing and its underlying mechanisms.

pmc-12767433.title: Bee Venom Acupuncture in the Treatment of Musculoskeletal System Disorders: A Comprehensive Review
pmc-12767433.creator: Xiaodi Zou, Yanzhao Dong, Ahmad Alhaskawi, Haiying Zhou, Sohaib Hasan Abdullah Ezzi, Vishnu Goutham Kota, Mohamed Hasan Abdulla Hasan Abdulla, Sahar Ahmed Abdalbary, Zhenfeng Liu, Changxin Wang, Hui Lu, Massimiliano Valeriani
pmc-12767433.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Disorders of the musculoskeletal system cover a broad spectrum of conditions that impact the muscles, skeletal structure, joints, tendons, and ligaments, leading to discomfort, swelling, and limited movement. Bee venom acupuncture (BVA), a practice commonly used in Asian countries, has been employed for a considerable time in traditional medicine systems to treat these disorders by utilizing bee venom and its main constituent, melittin.

pmc-13105870.title: Practical application of the BOPPPS model in infectious diseases education: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13105870.creator: Xiaohao Wang, Shan Zhong, Hu Li
pmc-13105870.description: BackgroundInfectious diseases education faces dual challenges: addressing knowledge sensitivity and bridging the theory-practice gap. Traditional didactic teaching inadequately cultivates both technical skills and humanistic literacy.ObjectiveTo evaluate the tripartite efficacy of the BOPPPS model in AIDS education, focusing on knowledge acquisition, skill-attitude integration, and learning experience.

pmc-13219287.title: Measuring attitudes toward artificial intelligence: validation of the Chinese ATTARI-12 and invariance across genders and academic disciplines
pmc-13219287.creator: Ping Li, Yong-Yee Chong, Wei Man, Hai Li
pmc-13219287.description: IntroductionUnderstanding university students’ attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI) is essential for its ethical and effective integration into higher education. However, validated tools tailored to the Chinese context are limited.MethodsThis study translated and validated the Chinese version of the Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence Scale (ATTARI-12) using Brislin’s translation procedure. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 920 undergraduate students.

pmc-13311086.title: Editorial: Microbial remediation of heavy metal pollution
pmc-13311086.creator: Iftikhar Ahmed, Alejandro Rodriguez-Sanchez, Duraipandiyan Veeramuthu, Pankaj Kumar Arora

pmc-13544950.title: Medial Swivel Injury: Misdiagnosis in Four Patients Over Three Months
pmc-13544950.creator: Alireza Mousavian, Yaghoob Keikha
pmc-13544950.description: Medial swivel injury is a rare injury among midfoot fracture-dislocations, typically caused by direct and high-energy force applied to the midfoot region. However, it can also develop after minor trauma, like a foot or ankle sprain sustained during sports or walking.
